---
title: "Learning and Game Design"
description: "Evidence-aware design knowledge for serious games about type 1 diabetes"
---

Start with the capability to be learned, not a reward system. This section connects player actions to learning mechanisms and tests.

1. [Learning science](learning-science.qmd): deliberate practice, explanatory feedback, scaffolding, retrieval and transfer.
2. [Game mechanisms](game-mechanisms.qmd): narrative, progression, rewards, autonomy and shared play.
3. [Evaluation](evaluation.qmd): outcomes, comparators, instruments and replication.
4. [Human factors](../human-factors/onboarding-and-accessibility.qmd): first-session design, emotional safety and accessibility.

For each feature, specify **what the learner does, what that activity should change and how the change will be measured**. Evidence labels are defined in [methods](../../methods.qmd); product implementations are compared in [design comparisons](../comparisons/comparative-analysis.qmd).
